title: Kemeny control
description: Can the chair delete a few voters (at most 'budget') so that the favourite tops a Kemeny ranking of the remaining ballots? This control problem is Sigma-2-complete (Fitzsimmons, Hemaspaandra, Hoover and Narvaez). The abstraction guesses the deleted voters and a ranking with the favourite on top, and the check a ranking closer to the remaining ballots; the refinement is a rule about distances, and the loop is Shape 4 (collect counterexamples, ground them in batches).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The election and the chair's favourite. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
voter(V) :- ballot(V,_).
rank(V,1,A) :- ballot(V,(A,_,_,_)).
rank(V,2,B) :- ballot(V,(_,B,_,_)).
rank(V,3,C) :- ballot(V,(_,_,C,_)).
rank(V,4,D) :- ballot(V,(_,_,_,D)).
% prefers(V,X,Y): voter V ranks X above Y.
prefers(V,X,Y) :- rank(V,I,X), rank(V,J,Y), I < J.
place(1..4).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): deleted voters and a ranking with the favourite on top.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most 'budget' deleted voters (a constant, set in the Loop tab) ...
{ del(V) : voter(V) } budget.
% ... and a ranking of the candidates with the favourite in first place.
1 { pos(X,P) : place(P) } 1 :- cand(X).
1 { pos(X,P) : cand(X) } 1 :- place(P).
:- favourite(X), not pos(X,1).
above(X,Y) :- pos(X,P), pos(Y,Q), P < Q.
#show del/1.
#show pos/2.

fragments.name: refine
fragments.description: Grounded once per counterexample: the candidate's ranking must not be further from the remaining ballots.
fragments.text:
% (k is the number of the counterexample here. Do not use k as a constant name in a
% project with a refine part: the constant would replace it.)
#program refine(k).
% cex(k,over(X,Y)): the k-th counterexample ranks X above Y. A ranking disagrees with
% a voter on a pair if it orders the pair the other way round. The candidate's ranking
% may not disagree more often with the remaining voters than the counterexample does.
:- #sum { 1,V,X,Y : prefers(V,X,Y), not del(V), cex(k,over(Y,X)) ;
         -1,V,X,Y : prefers(V,X,Y), not del(V), above(Y,X) } < 0.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted voters and the order of the ranking.
fragments.text:
glue(del(V)) :- voter(V).
glue(above(X,Y)) :- cand(X), cand(Y), X != Y.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a ranking that is closer to the remaining ballots (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: another ranking (any candidate may be on top) ...
1 { cpos(X,P) : place(P) } 1 :- cand(X).
1 { cpos(X,P) : cand(X) } 1 :- place(P).
over(X,Y) :- cpos(X,P), cpos(Y,Q), P < Q.
% ... that disagrees less often with the remaining voters than the candidate's ranking.
:- #sum { 1,V,X,Y : prefers(V,X,Y), not del(V), over(Y,X) ;
         -1,V,X,Y : prefers(V,X,Y), not del(V), above(Y,X) } >= 0.
#show over/2.
% No relevant/1 rules: the loop passes the ranking over/2 to the refine part.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

pending = []
repeat:
    search A:
        on candidate M:
            X = C.solve(assume G(M))
            if X:
                pending.push(X)
                reject M with G.block(M)
                if pending.size >= 20: restart
    grounded = pending.size
    for X in pending:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(over/2))
    pending.clear()
until A.exhausted and grounded == 0

instances.facts:
% An election with four candidates and seven voters; ballot(V,(A,B,C,D)): voter V
% ranks A first and D last.
cand(a;b;c;d).
ballot(1,(d,c,b,a)).
ballot(2,(a,c,d,b)).
ballot(3,(c,d,a,b)).
ballot(4,(b,d,c,a)).
ballot(5,(c,a,b,d)).
ballot(6,(a,d,c,b)).
ballot(7,(b,a,d,c)).
% The chair wants this candidate to win.
favourite(b).

% The election of the example with a budget of one deletion: not enough.
cand(a;b;c;d).
ballot(1,(d,c,b,a)).
ballot(2,(a,c,d,b)).
ballot(3,(c,d,a,b)).
ballot(4,(b,d,c,a)).
ballot(5,(c,a,b,d)).
ballot(6,(a,d,c,b)).
ballot(7,(b,a,d,c)).
% The chair wants this candidate to win.
favourite(b).

% The election of the example with a budget of three deletions.
cand(a;b;c;d).
ballot(1,(d,c,b,a)).
ballot(2,(a,c,d,b)).
ballot(3,(c,d,a,b)).
ballot(4,(b,d,c,a)).
ballot(5,(c,a,b,d)).
ballot(6,(a,d,c,b)).
ballot(7,(b,a,d,c)).
% The chair wants this candidate to win.
favourite(b).

% Nine voters; the favourite c is ranked last by four of them.
cand(a;b;c;d).
ballot(1,(a,b,c,d)).
ballot(2,(a,b,d,c)).
ballot(3,(b,a,d,c)).
ballot(4,(d,a,b,c)).
ballot(5,(c,d,a,b)).
ballot(6,(c,b,a,d)).
ballot(7,(b,c,d,a)).
ballot(8,(d,c,a,b)).
ballot(9,(a,c,b,d)).
favourite(c).

generators.name: ballots-ic
generators.description: An election under impartial culture: v voters, each ranks the four candidates a, b, c, d by a uniform permutation.
generators.text:
% ballots-ic: v voters; voter V ranks the candidates by a uniform permutation named V
cand(a;b;c;d).
c(1,a). c(2,b). c(3,c). c(4,d).
voter(1..v).
ballot(V,(A,B,C,D)) :- voter(V), c(@perm(4,1,V),A), c(@perm(4,2,V),B), c(@perm(4,3,V),C), c(@perm(4,4,V),D).
favourite(b).

#show cand/1.  #show ballot/2.  #show favourite/1.

generators.name: ballots-mallows
generators.description: An election under the Mallows model: rankings near a, b, c, d with dispersion phi/1000 (1000 = impartial culture).
generators.text:
% ballots-mallows: voter V places candidate I at position @mallows(4, phi, I, V)
cand(a;b;c;d).
c(1,a). c(2,b). c(3,c). c(4,d).
voter(1..v).
at(V,@mallows(4, phi, I, V),X) :- voter(V), c(I,X).
ballot(V,(A,B,C,D)) :- at(V,1,A), at(V,2,B), at(V,3,C), at(V,4,D).
favourite(b).

#show cand/1.  #show ballot/2.  #show favourite/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Ground every counterexample at once (Shape 3).
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(over/2))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

pending = []
repeat:
    search A:
        on candidate M:
            X = C.solve(assume G(M))
            if X:
                pending.push(X)
                reject M with G.block(M)
                if pending.size >= 5: restart
    grounded = pending.size
    for X in pending:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(over/2))
    pending.clear()
until A.exhausted and grounded == 0

library.summary: Deleting a few voters so that the favourite becomes a Kemeny winner; better rankings are collected and grounded in batches (Shape 4; 7 voters, budget = 2, 3 solutions).
